title: A Name C Will Accept
objective: Distinguish a C keyword from a valid identifier.
problem_statement: The program tries to use a C keyword as a variable name. Repair only the variable name so the program compiles and prints the student's age.
constraints:
• Keep the data type as int.
• Do not use a C keyword as the variable name.
• Keep the stored value 18.
• Print only the number.
hint_1: `while` already has a fixed meaning in C.
hint_2: Choose a normal identifier such as `age`.
success_message: You repaired a keyword/identifier mistake and kept the program's meaning unchanged.
technique_after_success: When renaming a variable, change every use of that identifier consistently.

title: One Character, Not a String
objective: Use single quotes for a character constant and double quotes for strings.
problem_statement: The variable is a char, but the starter code gives it a string constant. Fix the value so the program stores one character and prints it.
constraints:
• Keep the variable type char.
• Store the capital letter A.
• Use the correct quote style for a character constant.
• Print only A.
success_message: You separated a character constant from a string constant.
technique_after_success: When debugging quotes, first ask whether the code needs one character or a sequence of characters.

title: Keep the Fraction
objective: Choose a floating-point type when a fractional value must be preserved.
problem_statement: A price contains a fractional part. Repair the declaration and output so the program prints 75.84 exactly to two decimal places.
constraints:
• Store 75.84 as a floating-point value.
• Use double for the variable.
• Print exactly two digits after the decimal point.
• Output only the number.
hint_1: An int is for whole-number values.
hint_3: A double printed to two decimal places can use `%.2f`.
success_message: You chose a data type that preserves the fractional part of the value.
technique_after_success: Choose the type from the data you need to preserve, not from the shortest code you can write.

title: Give It a First Value
objective: Initialize an automatic local variable before reading it.
problem_statement: The program prints a local variable before giving it a known value. Initialize the variable so the program always prints 5.
constraints:
• Keep the variable name count.
• Keep the type int.
• Give count its value in the declaration.
• Print only 5.
hint_1: The variable exists, but what value does it have yet?
success_message: You prevented an uninitialized-variable bug by giving the local variable a known first value.
technique_after_success: Initialize local variables close to where they are declared when you already know the starting value.

title: Read Into the Right Place
objective: Use scanf with a matching integer format and the variable's address.
problem_statement: Read one integer from input and print the same integer back. Repair the scanf call so the input is stored in number.
constraints:
• Keep number as int.
• Use scanf with %d.
• Pass the address of number.
• Print only the integer that was entered.
hint_1: scanf needs to know where to store the input.
hint_2: For this int variable, use the address operator.
success_message: You connected formatted input to the memory location of an integer variable.
technique_after_success: When scanf behaves strangely, check the format specifier and the address argument as a pair.

title: Replace the Magic Number
objective: Use a symbolic constant for a repeated fixed value.
problem_statement: The program uses the fixed value 100 directly. Introduce the symbolic constant MAX with #define and print MAX.
constraints:
• Add `#define MAX 100` before main.
• Do not put a semicolon at the end of the #define line.
• Print the value through MAX.
• Output only 100.
hint_1: A symbolic constant is created before compilation.
success_message: You replaced an unexplained literal with a meaningful symbolic constant.
technique_after_success: Use symbolic names when the same fixed value has a clear meaning or may need to change in one place later.

title: Do Not Change const
objective: Respect a const-qualified variable after initialization.
problem_statement: The program declares class_size as const and then tries to change it. Repair the code so it compiles and prints the original class size.
constraints:
• Keep `const int class_size = 40;`.
• Do not cast away const.
• Remove the invalid modification.
• Print only 40.
hint_1: The declaration says this object should not be modified.
hint_2: The error is on the assignment after initialization.
success_message: You treated const as a real type qualifier rather than as a comment.
technique_after_success: If a value is conceptually fixed, make that rule visible in the type so accidental assignments are caught early.

title: Names That Describe States
objective: Use an enum to represent related named integer states.
problem_statement: Create an enum named state with OFF and ON. Print the value of ON using %d.
constraints:
• Declare `enum state {OFF, ON};`.
• Use the enumerator ON in the output.
• Do not replace ON with the raw number 1 in printf.
• Print only 1.
hint_1: By default the first enumerator is 0 and the next is 1.
hint_2: Define OFF first and ON second.
success_message: You replaced a raw state number with a readable named integer constant.
technique_after_success: Enums are useful when a variable represents one choice from a small named set of states.

title: Two Kinds of Input
objective: Combine integer and floating-point declarations with matching scanf formats.
problem_statement: Read a whole-number quantity and a real price, then print them as `quantity price` with the price shown to two decimal places.
constraints:
• quantity must be int.
• price must be double.
• Read both values with matching scanf formats.
• Print exactly: quantity, one space, price with two decimals.
hint_1: scanf can read more than one value in one call.
hint_2: For int use %d; for double input use %lf.
hint_3: Pass both variable addresses in the same order as the format specifiers.
success_message: You matched two different input formats with two different data types.
technique_after_success: For formatted input, read the format string left to right and match each conversion with the corresponding variable type and address.

title: Choose Enough Range
objective: Select a sufficiently wide integer type for a large fixed value.
problem_statement: Store the value 5000000000 in a variable named population and print it exactly. Use a long long integer and an LL literal suffix.
constraints:
• Declare population as long long.
• Use the literal 5000000000LL.
• Print with %lld.
• Output only the number.
hint_1: The chosen type should have enough range for the intended value.
hint_2: Use `long long` and the matching literal suffix.
success_message: You matched a large integer value with a wider integer type and matching format.
technique_after_success: When data can exceed an ordinary int range, design the type from the expected range instead of waiting for overflow bugs.
